extracted.intended_audience: general public; fans of comedy and pop-culture readers
extracted.subtask_description: A WatchMojo top-10 listicle that catalogs specific incidents in which comedians' actions or revelations tarnished their reputations and harmed their careers, with short explanations of the consequences for each person. The page uses examples to illustrate behaviors that led to lost roles, lost endorsements, cancellations, or long-term reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stephen Ranazzisi Lies About 9/11
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabricating a personal survival story about a major tragedy (claimed he was working in the South Tower on 9/11 and escaped) that was later exposed as false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New York Times exposed the lie in 2015; although he apologized, his career never really recovered — he went from starring on a successful TV show to mostly guest spots and podcast appearances. Example shows that dishonesty about traumatic events can permanently damage credibility and career prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shane Gillis' Racist Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Making racist and homophobic remarks publicly (recorded podcast comments) which surface when being considered for high-profile roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deep dive into his background revealed slurs; he was fired from SNL four days after being hired in 2019. He apologized and later found some success, but the revelations stalled TV prospects for years. Demonstrates that past recorded offensive content can derail major breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gilbert Gottfried's Insensitive Tweets
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting tasteless jokes about a natural disaster (tweets joking about the 2011 Japan earthquake and tsunami) that offend the public and corporate partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertiser Aflac dropped him as the voice of their duck mascot; while his movie/TV career continued, he lost commercial campaigns. Shows that public social-media insensitivity, especially about tragedies, can cost endorsements and commercial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charles Rocket Gets Fired
rubrics_metrics.description: Using profanity on network television (an on-air four-letter f-word on Saturday Night Live) and delivering unsatisfactory performance leading to dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNL discouraged hard cursing; Rocket's profanity and dissatisfaction with performance led to dismissal. It took years and smaller roles before steady work returned. Illustrates that violating broadcast norms or high-visibility slip-ups can result in immediate firing and career setbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jamie Kennedy's Disastrous Hosting Gig
rubrics_metrics.description: Poorly executed live/televised hosting (technical issues, unfunny jokes, offensive moments, missed countdown) that becomes widely derided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 2013 New Year's Eve special plagued with problems was dubbed 'the worst' by reporters; Kennedy later said the surreal tone was intentional but the episode damaged his profile and he hasn't had many high-profile roles since. Example of how a high-profile hosting failure can harm reputation and prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paul Reubens Arrested
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal conduct related to sexual indecency (arrested in an adult movie theater for indecent exposure) that prompts corporate and broadcast fallout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pee-wee toys were pulled, reruns canceled; although he continued working and later reprised the role successfully, the incident curtailed immediate opportunities. Demonstrates that arrests for sexual misconduct, especially connected to a children’s persona, can trigger rapid commercial removal and reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kathy Griffin's Presidential Photo
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating or publicizing an image perceived as violent or grotesque political provocation (posing with a photo suggesting she held the president's severed head).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues canceled tour dates, she lost her annual CNN New Year's Eve spot, and she was investigated by government officials. Griffin later turned the controversy into a self-referential tour and continued performing. Shows that extreme political provocation can lead to cancellations, investigations, and lost mainstream opportunities, though some artists may pivot from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Louis C.K. Admits to Misdeeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission or reporting of sexual misconduct by multiple women, leading to professional severing by networks and canceled releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a New York Times report with accusations, FX ceased working with him and his film's theatrical release was canceled. He later returned to performing independently and won a Grammy, but mainstream casting prospects remain uncertain. Highlights the severe industry consequences of sexual-misconduct revelations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roseanne Barr Loses Her Show
rubrics_metrics.description: Making an overtly racist public statement (tweet comparing Valerie Jarrett to an ape) that prompts network cancellation of a revived show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABC canceled the revival and replaced it with 'The Connors' without her; she was largely absent from TV and movies afterward aside from limited projects. Demonstrates that explicitly racist public remarks can lead to immediate cancellation and long-term exclusion from mainstream projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Michael Richards' Racist Tirade
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering an on-stage racist tirade at audience members during a stand-up performance, captured on video and widely publicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The incident at the Laugh Factory led to extensive media coverage; although he apologized, Richards' career never returned to prior heights — he retired from stand-up and had few credits afterward. Shows that public, recorded expressions of racism during performances can cause lasting career collapse.
